text: Every lesson so far in this chapter has described roles and responsibilities in prose. This lesson gives you the tool that makes all of it precise, on paper: the RACI matrix.

RACI is four letters crossed against a list of tasks. R is Responsible — does the actual work. A is Accountable — owns the outcome, with final sign-off, and there should be exactly one A per task. C is Consulted — gives input before a decision. And I is Informed — kept aware after the fact, one-way.

Map that onto the roles you already know. The owner is typically Accountable. The steward is Responsible for daily work. The custodian is Responsible specifically for technical implementation tasks. And the consumer is usually just Informed — aware of the outcome without driving the decision.

Here's the one rule that keeps a RACI matrix useful instead of decorative: exactly one A per row. Two people both marked Accountable for the same task isn't clarity — it's the ambiguity you were trying to fix, written back down on paper. And notice the A can legitimately shift by task: the owner holds it for approving a rule, but the custodian holds it for implementing that rule correctly.
One grid, four letters, one A per row. Next lesson covers the role that makes this entire chapter's structure actually stick inside a real organization: executive sponsorship. See you there.
